oracle.historical_exposure: The generator predates this review and its --write produced the pinned numbers; its author is the repository author. Whether the author had seen the production implementation, and whether the in-test closed-form code was derived from this generator or the reverse, is unrecorded.
oracle.independence_basis: The retained generator is standard-library Python with a PEP 723 header that imports no Antecedent code. It evaluates the Gaussian truncated-mean closed form, solves the discrete Riccati fixed point and forms the gain and the open-loop optimum by hand, then cross-checks the treatment and closed-loop values against its own seeded Monte Carlo with a separate generator and dynamics. The shared objects are the stated model (stage utility u(z - k); linear dynamics with quadratic cost) and its parameters, which the generator echoes and the test hard-codes separately.
oracle.method: treat-above-threshold optimum for a stationary Gaussian state and the linear-quadratic Riccati feedback optimum with the closed-form best open-loop schedule

reference_review.limitations: The test compares its own in-test closed-form code with this document, so agreement shows the two implementations of the same formulas match, not that a policy-search run reaches the optimum; the Monte Carlo cross-check is a 0.05 and 0.3 absolute band on a seeded run. The generator regenerates the numeric blocks with --write but keeps the recorded oracle block; a rewrite that changes any numeric value makes the review stale. No calibration claim.
